references.text: Moses' sister, probably Miriam, had stood at a distance to see what would happen to the child, and now she seizes the opportunity to help.
Pharaoh's daughter accepts the sister's suggestion, and Moses' own mother is brought in to nurse him, fulfilling the sister's plan.
Miriam is identified here as Aaron's sister and a prophetess, and is traditionally regarded as the sister who spoke to Pharaoh's daughter.
Jochebed is mentioned as the mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, confirming the family relationship and that it was Moses' own mother who became his nurse.
By faith Moses was hidden by his parents for three months, and God's providence worked through the sister's initiative to preserve the child.
Both verses highlight the remarkable vitality and survival ability of the Hebrew women in Egypt.
